set.approach: From a campsite at Peeler Lake, walk up a grassy drainage to the east and the wall appears on the left. Ledges form the lower half of the wall and can be scrambled to the halfway ledge where the main-section routes begin. Bold Deceiver climbs the two striking cracks in the orange face at the right-hand end of the main wall.
set.descent_text: Belay on gear at the top, then walk left to the main ledge and follow the walk-off. Walk off down the gully between the two subsections of the wall.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route and wall pages. One source each, so medium.

set.descent_text: Belay on gear above the corner and walk off to the left.

set.approach: From a campsite at Peeler Lake, walk up a grassy drainage to the east and the wall appears on the left. Ledges form the lower half of the wall and can be scrambled to the halfway ledge where the main-section routes begin. Stand and Deliver is the middle line of the right-hand section: scramble up to the main ledge, then look for the shallow corner facing left just to the right of the big pine in the center of the face.
set.descent_text: Belay from the lodgepole at the top; the formation tops out after an easy traverse left. Walk off down the gully between the two subsections of the wall.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route and wall pages. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Drive to the top of Pine Creek where the pack station is, and start up the Pine Creek Pass trail. Pipe Wall sits beside the trail and is the first of the Brownstone walls you meet. Starting from the big slab at the foot of the wall, scramble up and to the right, past a corner facing right, to the foot of the next corner; the route is the thin crack in the left side of that corner's left wall.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: From the southern parking lot at the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, walk east from the fence line to a south-facing formation with a single bolt in the middle of its face. New Pygmy goes up the layered plates at the formation's left end and finishes on a slab.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: From the southern parking lot at the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, walk east from the fence line to a south-facing formation with a single bolt in the middle of its face. Watusi Rodeo follows the seam that angles up and left on the right side of the formation.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: There are two ways in. The direct one follows the approach used for the Mean Streak wall, then cuts left up to the base of the buttress. The longer, gentler one climbs the Pine Creek Pass trail to the Brownstone buttress, leaves the trail slightly downhill at the end of the long switchback below it, crosses Pine Creek below the waterfall, and heads up the open shelf that cuts up right toward the buttress, following occasional cairns across open ground. The route is the obvious lightning-bolt dihedral in the middle of the white quartz-streaked buttress.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from its anchors back to the ground.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Follow the well-kept Wapama Falls trail around Hetch Hetchy Reservoir, and the slab lies some distance before Rancheria Falls. The last stretch up to the base is a steep bushwhack along faint deer trails, and poison oak is common even beside the main trails. The girdle begins at a big pine at the slab's left end; an easy fourth-class ramp leads to the slab itself.
set.descent_text: The line ends at a large pine tree; exit down a small vegetated ramp or gully.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The Rectory is the most striking formation visible from the end of the fire road, and the walk in is over easy terrain. Look for a cairn marking a trail where the approach steepens; there are also many ways to reach the base over bare rock. Going My Way is the obvious crack on the west face, left of the pine tree that Stairway to Heaven passes.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Talus below the tower scrambles easily to its foot, and the route begins right at the toe.
set.descent_text: Rappel the line of the route back to the base. From the top, the first rappel goes south, over the ledge below the lower summit, to an anchor on a stance; after that, descend straight down the face. Any anchors you passed with rappel rings on the way up are part of this line.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: The buttress sits east of the Needles, across the Kern River canyon. Hike the Schaffer Meadow Trail to about Cedar Canyon, then drop down to the wall. The start is in a scooped-out recess of brown blocks and cracks that look solid but questionable.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Turn onto Running Springs School Road, drive to the unmarked gated dirt road on the left, and walk it, then a vague trail, a short way to the base of the crag. It is a west-facing formation above the town of Running Springs. Flake of Flakes is a thin left-facing flake far to the right on the crag, right of Changing Corners.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Turn onto Running Springs School Road, drive to the unmarked gated dirt road on the left, and walk it, then a vague trail, a short way to the base of the crag. It is a west-facing formation above the town of Running Springs. Nursery Time lies round the corner to the left of Twin Cracks, on the rock's northwest side; it climbs a flake and then bolted face.
set.descent_text: Walk off, or rappel from one of the anchors on top of the west face.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

It is a west-facing formation above the town of Running Springs. Primary Grades starts from the ledge a short way left of Flake of Flakes and climbs a right-facing corner system.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Park where Greenway Drive ends at Pioneer Lane, then take trails up the steep rocky hillside past The Gardens toward the Upper Hill blocks. Secret Spot Rock is a big block tucked among trees straight uphill from Shark Fin. Dirty Little Secret is on the left side of its south face.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Leave the Lake George parking area and walk the left-hand shoreline to the lake's far side, where a climbers trail climbs the hillside to the cliff. Continue past the established routes on the north face of the Dike Wall to Sector Mellow, the first slab you reach. Sector Evil Seed is a scramble up and right above it, so watch for loose talus and rock. The squeeze crack is the trad line in Sector Evil Seed.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: From the east, begin at the Pine Creek Pass trailhead and walk the Pine Creek Pass trail beyond Upper Pine Lake, branching toward Honeymoon Lake. Carry on through Granite Park to the crest, which you cross at Granite Bear Pass, south of Italy Pass beside Granite Park Spire. Go west cross-country into the Bear Lakes area, passing Big Bear Lake on its north and Little Bear Lake on its south, then trend southwest past tarns to Vee Lake. Walk down its outlet to the East Fork of Bear Creek and work uphill cross-country to the peak. The route is the leftmost gable on the north face.

review.notes: Peak approach from the area page; the route page places the line on the north face. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Hike the Robinson Creek Trail beyond Barney Lake toward the junction for Peeler and Robinson Lakes; the small wall is right beside the trail on the left. Hypnocrunch is slightly downhill from one of the switchbacks and is hard to miss. Begin with an undercling off to the right of the crack's line, then move left into it.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts from its own page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, over New or Old Army Pass, or over Arc Pass, with good camping anywhere along the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond is the steep, clean, diamond-shaped shield due south of Sky Blue Lake: counting from the far left, it is the fourth of the walls and towers leading up to the lake. Altared State is right of the A-frame crack that splits the headwall and follows a clean right-facing crack system across the shield. From the base, scramble to a broad ledge running across the formation's right side; a brief fourth-class step guards access to it.
set.descent_text: A huge ledge below the summit can be walked off to the right (north), and non-technical terrain leads all the way back to the base. From the summit, reverse the route down to that ledge by downclimbing and a couple of rappels; the summit block itself has a low fifth-class move to reverse.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, over New or Old Army Pass, or over Arc Pass, with good camping anywhere along the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond is the steep, clean, diamond-shaped shield due south of Sky Blue Lake: counting from the far left, it is the fourth of the walls and towers leading up to the lake. Journey to the Center of the Earth follows one long splitter crack through the middle of the Diamond's tallest section, entering the left side of the big alcove roughly two-thirds of the way up and climbing through it.
set.descent_text: Scramble down west toward Primrose Lake, or retrace the route by rappelling and downclimbing from the summit to the big ledge partway up, then head right back into Miter Basin. A large ledge partway up also allows an escape off to the right.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.approach: Approach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, over New or Old Army Pass, or over Arc Pass, with good camping anywhere along the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond is the steep, clean, diamond-shaped shield due south of Sky Blue Lake: counting from the far left, it is the fourth of the walls and towers leading up to the lake. Spankin' the Marmot sits at the left end of the Diamond, on a tidy vertical splitter that bends left into a tall dihedral. The first section is a scramble up stepped ledges and corners to the foot of the headwall, with access from the far-left gully.
set.descent_text: Either scramble down the back toward Primrose Lake, or reverse the route (with some rappelling) to the walk-off ledge, then go right and scramble down toward Sky Blue Lake.

set.approach: Approach as for the Mammoth Peak Alcove: on Tioga Road westbound, park at the gravel pull-off a little past the Mono Pass trailhead lot, cross the river, and head through trees to the alcove. From there skirt the base eastward until you reach a prominent buttress cut by cracks, where a mixed line begins at the foot. Flyin' High is left of center on the buttress, just right of Mr. Blue Sky, and climbs bolts to a big diagonal V-shaped slot.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from the ring anchors.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.

set.descent_text: Rappel from the ring anchor at the top, knotting the rope ends.

set.approach: From the base of the west face of Parking Lot Rock, follow the trail that wraps around its north side and then heads north; the Slack Wall is a few minutes along. From Two Tree Rock you can instead walk south along its base. The route is at the short, right-hand end of the cove.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor at the top.

review.notes: Crag access from the area page; where this line starts and how it is descended from the route page. One source each, so medium.
